record.context_brief: Failure when λ is not strong limit
record.original_question: If λ is singular and not a strong limit cardinal, does ZFC prove the negative relation \((λ^+ over λ) ↛ (λ^+ over λ)^(1,1)_2\)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.11. Is it provable in ZFC that (λ^+ over λ) ↛ (λ^+ over λ)^(1,1)_2 whenever λ > cf(λ) and λ is not strong limit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, write $\binom{\alpha}{\beta} \to \binom{\gamma}{\delta}^{1,1}_2$ for the polarized partition relation asserting that for every coloring $c : \alpha \times \beta \to 2$ there exist $A \subseteq \alpha$ and $B \subseteq \beta$ with order types $\gamma$ and $\delta$ respectively such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$. Write $\binom{\alpha}{\beta} \not\to \binom{\gamma}{\delta}^{1,1}_2$ for its negation.

Let $\lambda$ be a singular cardinal (so $\mathrm{cf}(\lambda) < \lambda$) that is not a strong limit cardinal (i.e., there exists $\mu < \lambda$ with $2^\mu \geq \lambda$). 

Question: Does ZFC prove that
$$\binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \not\to \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 ?$$
artifact.category_tag: polarized partition relations on singular cardinals
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a clear resolution of this specific question about the negative polarized partition relation at a singular non-strong-limit cardinal $\lambda$ in ZFC. Related results on polarized relations at singular cardinals exist in the literature, but none directly confirm or refute provability in ZFC of the displayed negative relation under the stated hypotheses.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in singular cardinal combinatorics, including partition relations.
status_evidence.claim: The general area contains many open ZFC questions about partition relations at singular cardinals.

status_evidence.title: A strong polarized relation
status_evidence.snippet: Consistency results on polarized partition relations at singular cardinals.
status_evidence.claim: Polarized partition relations at singular cardinals depend on cardinal arithmetic assumptions; ZFC-provability statements are sensitive to whether the cardinal is a strong limit.
